# 1 Introduction

This Section establishes a framework and controls to guide development on land within the Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts.


# 1.1 Land to which this Section applies

This section applies to certain land within the Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts, as shown in Figure 1 below.

![page 4 img 1 (1142x1615)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0004-40d28cbd1f50.png)


*Figure 1:*

Land to which this Section applies ( Note : Excludes SSDA land shown as red hatched area)


<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 5 -->

Substantial areas of these precincts are subject to State Significant Development Applications (SSDAs). These areas have been identified as red hatched areas in Figure 1 . Urban Design Guidelines, approved by the Department of Planning and Environment (the Department) as part of the SSDAs, will guide future development on the applicable SSDA land (as shown in Figure 2 ). Therefore, this DCP does not apply to these areas. The approval pathway for SSDA land is further detailed below.

Various pockets of non-SSDA land also have limited development potential, whether it is due to the current planning controls, proximity to the Metro and arterial road, fragmented land ownership or ecological constraints due to proximity to the Elizabeth Macarthur Creek Riparian Corridor. The controls under this DCP are applicable to the land not covered by the SSDAs, which is primarily the 'development lots' identified in Figure 1 , along with some land in the immediate vicinity of these lots.


*Figure 2:*

Overview of applicable guidelines


# 1.2 Purpose of this Section

The purpose of this section of the DCP is to guide the future development of the Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts by identifying the vision, development principles, key elements and indicative structure for the future development of the precinct. It seeks to ensure the orderly, efficient and environmentally sensitive development of the precinct to achieve high quality urban design outcomes.

This DCP was developed with consideration to the Apartment Design Guide, which sets minimum requirements for apartment building development. This DCP builds on these same principles to facilitate the delivery of a distinct local character that aligns with Council's vision for the Precinct.


# 1.3 Relationship to other Sections of the DCP

This section forms part of The Hills Development Control Plan 2012 (DCP 2012). Development within the Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts will need to have regard to this section of the DCP as well as other relevant controls in DCP 2012. In the event of any inconsistency between this section and other sections of DCP 2012, this section will prevail to the extent of the inconsistency.


<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 6 -->

Note . Refer to Part B Section 8 - Shop Top Housing and Mixed Use Development for development controls pertaining to shops, restaurants or cafes or business premises on the ground floor of shop top housing and mixed use developments in the R4 High Density Residential zone.


# 1.4 Approval Pathway for SSDA Land

The SSDA applications (SSD-10344, SSD-10343) for a concept master plan, urban design guidelines and Stage 1 subdivision of public open space lots are currently under assessment by the Department of Planning and Environment and are available for viewing on the Department's 'Major Projects' website ( drafting note : the final determination status will be reflected here, once the applications have been finalised and before any finalisation/adoption of this DCP document). Future applications will be required to facilitate further subdivision and the detailed design and construction of buildings, open space, public domain areas and associated civil infrastructure and works.

Under Schedule 2 of the State Environmental Planning Policy (Planning Systems) 2021 (formerly the State Environmental Planning Policy (State and Regional Development) 2011), the following types of development are identified as State Significant Development within the Bella Vista and Kellyville Precincts:

- A principal subdivision establishing major lots or public domain areas, or
- The creation of new roadways and associated works.
The Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 permits a consent authority, in assessing a concept SSDA, to determine the future stages of development that are to be assessed by Council and that cease to be State Significant. Landcom has requested that the criteria for future applications to be considered State Significant include:

-  A principal subdivision establishing major lots or public domain areas;
-  The creation of new roadways and associated works; or
-  Has a capital investment value of more than $30 million.
Landcom's Concept SSDAs, including the supporting Urban Design Guidelines, are intended to serve as the primary guiding policy for future development within the SSDA boundaries. The Urban Design Guidelines provide site-specific development controls that future development will be required to comply with and they guide the detailed landscape and architectural design within the approved SSDA open space network, street network, lot structure and building envelopes. The Urban Design Guidelines are also proposed to be supported by a Design Excellence Process, which includes referral to a State Design Review Panel (separate to Council's process) to ensure design quality is maintained through the life of the project (including beyond the initial divestment stage).


<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 7 -->


# 2 Vision and Principles


# 2.1 Vision

The Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts are envisaged to transform into an attractive and wellconnected neighbourhood that achieves housing targets, creates vibrant, safe and desirable places, reinforces the garden Shire character and lifestyle and is supported by necessary infrastructure. It is anticipated that the precincts will provide around 8,400 dwellings and 10,400 jobs by 2036 (noting that a majority of this uplift will be located on SSDA land). In order to meet this vision, future development within the Precincts must achieve the following key principles and strategic priorities.

![page 7 img 1 (1043x739)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0007-dc6fb9ae7a09.png)


*Figure 3:*

Visualisation of the Kellyville Station Precinct

(Source: Updated Urban Design Report submitted in association with the Kellyville SSDA prepared by SJB Urban)


# 2.2 Development Principles

To achieve the vision, future development within the Precinct must address the following key principles and strategic priorities of Council:


## Housing Diversity

As the population grows there will be greater reliance on higher density development to accommodate future housing demand. The expected characteristics of the Hills Shire population will continue to include a variety of household types including singles, couples and a high proportion of households with children. It will be critical that future high density development provides 'dwelling diversity' to ensure the market caters for the different living needs, expectations and household budgets within the community. This will require the provision of an appropriate mix of one, two and three bedroom apartments which are varied in size.


<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 8 -->

Apartment buildings are long term building stock so it is very important that if they are to be built, they are resilient over the long term. Unlike detached housing where landowners can choose the style and size of their home, a homeowner wanting an apartment can only choose from what is being provided. Whilst smaller apartments should be provided to meet the needs of a certain demographic within the market, moderate and larger apartments should also be provided to meet the latent demand for this housing option. This will then reduce pressure on smaller, more affordable housing options.

![page 8 img 1 (763x316)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0008-9df849e53ea0.png)


*Figure 4:*

Council's Approach to Housing Diversity

![page 8 img 2 (377x274)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0008-a8ed5b4e85cc.png)

![page 8 img 3 (379x275)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0008-22f270a696f8.png)


*Figure 5:*

Examples of Diverse Housing Products

(Source: Urban Design Report submitted in association with the Bella Vista SSDA prepared by Hassell, 2019)


## Employment Outcomes

The Bella Vista and Kellyville Precincts are strategically located in close proximity to the Norwest Strategic Centre, which is set to transform into a thriving commercial office precinct that serves the rapidly growing North West Region. Given it is earmarked for significant employment growth, it is crucial that employment lands be maintained and protected to ensure that job targets within our key strategic planning documents can be achieved.


<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 9 -->

It is envisaged that future employment growth will be tailored to the needs of our highly skilled and educated workforce, to provide an array of jobs close to home as we continue to strive towards a '30 minute city'. However, at present a large proportion of residents are travelling outside The Hills Shire to pursue employment opportunities, notable in occupations such as 'professionals', 'managers' or 'clerical and administrative workers'. The Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts essentially present a blank canvas that can springboard off the Norwest Business Park and the arrival of the Sydney Metro North West, to evolve into a thriving and competitive employment destination. It also presents an opportunity to address the current imbalance between the available jobs and the skills of residents, and ensure that new populations can access high quality professional employment close to where they live.

Establishing a sense of place and night-time economy will be key drawcards in attracting employees and also in encouraging businesses to invest in the area. The planning controls will further attract businesses by facilitating quality spaces and facilities for workers and visitors including active streets that promote commercial, retail and business activity and town squares and plazas that provide spaces for informal meetings, recreation and dining.

![page 9 img 1 (356x192)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0009-3c410edfb693.png)


*Figure 6:*

Examples of Town Squares (left) and Employment Areas (right)

(Source: Urban Design Report submitted in association with the Bella Vista SSDA prepared by Hassell, 2019)


## Transit Oriented Development

Transit oriented development (TOD) involves the creation of compact, walkable, mixed-use communities around public transport nodes. A key goal of TODs is to increase the number of people who walk, cycle or use public transport as their main form of transport. TODs have densities that result in increased patronage of public transport and provide more opportunities for people to live near the station and reduce their reliance on vehicles.

The need to locate high density housing in centres with good access to services, community facilities and transport is well recognised and will support the on-going operation of the Sydney Metro Northwest. Density at the core allows for a scale and character suitable for pedestrian connectivity. Centres should provide a mixture of residential, retail and commercial activities that are centred on transport and create an environment where services, recreation, entertainment, jobs and housing provide a lifestyle alternative to the traditional suburban context, consistent with the principles of TODs.

![page 9 img 2 (376x272)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0009-6a09bed9f601.png)


<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 10 -->

This DCP Section supports the provision of TODs by helping to deliver the highest densities in key strategic locations close to centres and existing and proposed transport infrastructure. This will ensure a sensible balance can be achieved between delivering on housing targets whilst ensuring an appropriate transition in residential densities and maintaining residential character.

![page 10 img 1 (677x452)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0010-8b150ad3f0a0.png)


*Figure 7:*

![page 10 img 2 (674x452)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0010-b03fae8df37e.png)

Bella Vista Metro Station and Surrounds (Source: THSC)


## Infrastructure and Open Space

Public open spaces play an important role in urban areas including provision of recreation, environmental conservation, connecting people with nature and improving social connectivity and mental health.

The expected additional population of approximately 13,850 people within the Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts will increase demand for various public facilities and services (such as roads, community facilities, open space and the like). This future population should be provided with access to open space, recreation and community facilities in line with the lifestyle enjoyed by existing residents.

There is a need to vastly improve open space networks to meet the demands generated by incoming population and ensure appropriate recreational opportunities are provided for the future population. A number of local and neighbourhood parks are required in key locations that will be connected through dedicated shared ways along all streets providing a high level of amenity for both pedestrian and cyclists. Public plazas and town squares in the areas surrounding the stations and upgrades to open spaces outside of the precincts provide further opportunities for active and passive recreation.


<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 11 -->

![page 11 img 1 (444x241)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0011-2c64cfea41bd.png)


*Figure 8:*

![page 11 img 2 (442x242)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0011-a2067e9b8f2c.png)

Example of Open Space Areas

(Source: Urban Design Report submitted in association with the Bella Vista SSDA prepared by Hassell, 2019)


## Place Making

Place making will be a key focus in order to provide neighbourhoods that are sustainable, accessible, safe, attractive and well serviced with a unique character and sense of place. The development controls will provide the ingredients that make neighbourhoods liveable including vibrant activity centres, permeable and safe movement networks, generous public spaces, high quality built form and public art and ecologically sustainable development. The provision of quality spaces including streets, parks, buildings, and other public spaces will invite greater interaction between people and foster healthier, more social and economically viable communities.

Public areas such as informal gathering areas within centres will include high quality and durable elements such as seating, shading and lighting to enhance the amenity of these areas. Streets will be well connected incorporating shared pedestrian/cycleways. The precinct will incorporate new public domain treatments including new paving, new street furniture and lighting, improved pedestrian access and dedicated street tree planting.

Quality built form plays a vital role in achieving liveable, productive and resilient environments and creating great places that people want to live, work, visit and invest in. Development which achieves the key principles and meets with the development controls in this DCP will ensure an exemplary standard of design that provides a positive contribution to the public realm. A design excellence clause has also been included within The Hills Local Environmental Plan 2019 to require certain buildings to be assessed by a design excellence panel to achieve quality built form outcomes for the precincts.

# 3 Desired Future Character and Structure Plans


# 3.1 Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts

The Bella Vista Station Precinct is bound by Celebration Drive to the south, Elizabeth Macarthur Creek to the east, Memorial Avenue to the north and Old Windsor Road to the west. It is also dissected by two (2) key roads, being Balmoral Road and Mawson Avenue.

The Kellyville Station Precinct is bound by Memorial Avenue to the south, Elizabeth Macarthur Creek to the east, Samantha Riley Drive to the north and Old Windsor Road to the west.

However, this DCP only applies to non-SSDA land (as previously shown in Figure 1 ).


# 3.2 Character Areas

Whilst the Bella Vista Precinct is a highly diverse precinct, given this DCP section only relates to the non-SSDA land, two (2) key character areas have been identified:


## Residential Areas

Residential areas will be highly desirable and accessible, providing a range of housing choices that meets the diverse needs of our local residents. Development will also feature transit oriented design principles, whereby the area will be highly walkable, with generous street setbacks for pedestrians, and importantly, taller buildings will be concentrated towards the station tapering down to the wellestablished low density areas.

![page 12 img 1 (874x317)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0012-4ba568a81221.png)

![page 12 img 2 (426x311)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0012-30e3667fce5a.png)

![page 12 img 3 (433x329)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0012-e48fd88b93a9.png)

Built Form Example within Residential Area

(Source: Urban Design Report submitted in association with the Bella Vista SSDA prepared by Hassell, 2019)


<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 13 -->


## Elizabeth Macarthur Creek Corridor Character

The Elizabeth Macarthur Creek Corridor will be a key defining feature that will be showcased through future development within the precinct. It is set to transform into a space that offers a variety of recreational and lifestyle opportunities for the enjoyment of local residents and workers, including walkways and cycleways that connect into the broader network, providing quality connections within and around the precinct.

![page 13 img 1 (377x422)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0013-c821dd5b7fb0.png)

# 3.3 Structure Plans and Key Elements


# Objectives

- To provide a mix of housing and services within the Precincts (that supports the broader employment and mixed use areas located within the SSDA areas).
- To ensure that development occurs in a coordinated manner consistent with the vision and development principles for the Precincts.
- To locate higher density outcomes closer to the station to optimise access to the station facilities as well as outlook and amenity.

# Controls

- Development is to be consistent with the desired character outlined in Section 3.2 of this DCP, the key elements in Table 1 and the structure plans in Figures 12 and 13 .
- Where variations are proposed, development is to demonstrate how the vision, development principles, key elements for the Precincts and relevant specific objectives are to be achieved.
![page 13 img 3 (376x418)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0013-e4d73541032f.png)


<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 14 -->

Table 1 Key Elements of the Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts

| Element                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Land Use                     |  Bella Vista: Residential areas comprise higher density built form in the southern non-SSDA areas, transitioning to lower scale apartments further north towards Memorial Avenue and further east towards Elizabeth Macarthur Creek Corridor.  Kellyville: Low and mid-rise apartment buildings located along the Elizabeth Macarthur Creek Corridor and on the southern side of Sanctuary Drive near the T-way stop.                                                                                                                           |
| Built Form                   |  High quality architectural and urban design.  Bella Vista: Taller apartment buildings of up to 8 storeys located in the southern non-SSDA areas. Lower apartment buildings of up to 6 storeys located towards Memorial Avenue and the Elizabeth Macarthur Creek Corridor.  Kellyville: Heights transitioning to 10 storeys south of the station towards Memorial Avenue. Lower apartment buildings of up to 6 storeys located the Elizabeth Macarthur Creek Corridor.  Parks and other key public domain areas protected from overshadowing. |
| Open Space and Public Domain |  Various local parks distributed throughout the residential areas.  Open space (such as pocket parks) integrated within the Elizabeth Macarthur Creek Corridor where possible and passive open space is located underneath the Metro Line.  Improved access and crossings between the Precinct and the Elizabeth Macarthur Creek Corridor.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Movement Network             |  Precinct is bound by two key arterial roads, including Old Windsor Road to the west and Memorial Avenue to the north.  Various new connections are proposed to enhance access and permeability including new roads south of Memorial Avenue (building upon the local road network proposed as part of the SSDA).  New and upgraded shared paths along key routes and new cycleways associated with Elizabeth Macarthur Creek and connecting open spaces.                                                                                      |

# 4 General Controls


# 4.1 Movement Network and Design


# Objectives

- To encourage residents to walk or cycle to shops, the railway station, recreation areas, community and other facilities by providing for safe and direct pedestrian and cycle connections between key locations.
- A functional and attractive new street network is provided that facilitates access, safety and convenience for all street and road users and minimises the negative impact of traffic.
- Carriageways and verge widths are consistent with the identified street hierarchy and sections to allow streets to perform their designated functions within the street network, enhance functionality and amenity for users and accommodate public utilities and drainage systems.
- Improve the capacity and function of the road network to support higher density development.
- Encourage orderly development that appropriately integrates with planned development in the surrounding areas.

# Controls

- The street network must be consistent with the indicative street network and hierarchy shown in Figure 17 .
- Street profiles for non-SSDA land are subject to the controls shown in Figures 19 - 22 .
- Appropriate transitions and connectivity must be provided between roads constructed throughout the Precincts (including those constructed by different parties).
- The design and construction of road infrastructure shall comply with Council's Design Guidelines Subdivisions/Developments.
- Where roundabouts are provided, these are to be appropriately landscaped to ensure visibility for traffic and high quality visual amenity (refer Figures 14 and 15 ).
- All roads (including cul-de-sacs) must be constructed to specifications that will facilitate the efficient movement of waste and service vehicles.
- Road infrastructure not funded through a Contributions Plans is to be constructed to Council's specifications and dedicated to Council at no cost.
- The cycleway network is to be consistent with the proposed cycleway network under Contributions Plan No. 18 - Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts (as shown in Figure 18 ).
- To maximise the pedestrian experience, vehicular and loading access to residential developments is to be provided via mid-block (east west) roads, where possible.
- Through site links (east west) are to be provided to increase pedestrian permeability in the precincts, and to provide increased connectivity from residential areas to the riparian corridor.
- Future development must ensure there are no impediments to maintenance access areas for the Sydney Metro North West Rail Corridor.

<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 18 -->

- As part of the lodgement of any future development application, the Applicant is to prepare and submit documentation compliant with the Sydney Metro At Grade and Elevated Sections Corridor Protection Guidelines (available from www.sydneymetro.info).
- Direct vehicular access to arterial roads will not be permitted where alternate access is available. Access will not be restricted to any property with existing access from arterial roads until such time as alternate access is available'. This control will reflect the existing control within the Balmoral Road Release Area DCP.

# 4.2 Public Domain


# Objectives

- To provide a range of quality public spaces to support future development.
- To improve the quality and aesthetic of the public domain to reflect the transitioning of the Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts into a Transit Orientated Community.
- To provide an improved pedestrian experience.
- To ensure the provision of high quality, functional and attractive informal spaces for community interaction and play are provided.
- Undergrounding of power lines to improve the aesthetics and liveability of the centre and to facilitate increased space within road reserves to install public domain improvements.

# Controls

- Attractive, high quality outdoor spaces for children to play should be integrated into the public domain within centres where appropriate. Such spaces should allow for interactive play and include seating and shading.
- Council requires underground electricity reticulation and telecommunications for all urban development. Council will require as a condition of any development consent that any existing aboveground electricity reticulation service be relocated underground with the exception of main transmission lines.
- Underground of electricity reticulation and telecommunications should also be subject to the asset owner's approval/concurrence from the relevant electricity authority/asset owner.
- Pedestrian laneways and through site links shall have high regard to the following:
-  Being publicly accessible;
-  Have a minimum width of 4.5 metres;
-  Be clearly identifiable as a publicly accessible pedestrian link;
-  Encourage pedestrian movement along the link and minimise crowding;
-  Maintain the privacy of ground floor residential apartments which adjoin the link;
-  Ensure adequate passive surveillance is provided;
-  Have adequate lighting to improve safety; and
-  Building setbacks to the pedestrian link are to be assessed on their merits.
- Incorporate effective and clear way finding to ensure efficient movement throughout the Precincts.
- High quality landscaping and tree canopy cover should be integrated into the public domain and any through site links.
- Permeable surfaces should also be provided where possible to reduce the extent of paved area and to enhance the amenity of the streetscape environment.

# 4.3 Integrated Water Management


## Objectives

- To control stormwater runoff and discharge impacts on adjoining properties and into natural drainage systems before, during and after construction.
- To ensure that proposed development does not adversely affect the operation capacity of the downstream stormwater system.
- To encourage reuse, recycling and harvesting of stormwater to reduce demand on potable water supply.
![page 27 img 4 (1015x675)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0027-0acd286bae9b.png)


<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 28 -->

- To encourage and create an urban form where risks to life and property, as a result of either minor or major flooding, are minimised.
- To maximise opportunities for a best practice Water Sensitive Urban Design approach at the individual lot, overall development and regional scales.
- To reduce the impacts typically associated with urbanisation on receiving waterways, including a reduction in streamflow erosion potential and pollutant loads.

## Controls

- Owners of properties adjoining the riparian corridor and overland flow paths as well as properties identified as Flood Control Lots are required to confirm the 100 year Average Recurrence Interval flood extent and associated flood levels from the riparian corridor prior to the lodgment of development and subdivision applications.
- Development on land identified as Flood Control Lots and adjoining Elizabeth Macarthur Creek or overland flow paths are to apply the provisions of Council's Flood Controlled Land DCP. In applying these provisions consideration is to be given to the type of development, the application of controls according to the Flood Planning Level associated with the property, car parking, flood compatible building materials and land filling.
- A Stormwater Management Plan is to be prepared for each development application that considers sustainable water management practices and minimal development impact.
- Stormwater runoff must be treated on the development site before it discharges to a public drainage system.
- All stormwater drainage designs are to comply with the most up to date revision of Council's Design Guidelines Subdivision/Developments and Contribution Plan No.18 - Bella Vista and Kellyville Station Precincts.
- All developments are to implement an Erosion and Sediment Control Plan, prepared in accordance with 'Managing Urban Stormwater - Soils and Construction, to minimise land disturbance and erosion and control sediment pollution of waterways.
- With the exclusion of detached residential dwellings, all developments within the Precinct are required to manage the pollutant loads from each separate allotment to ensure compliance with the performance objective listed in Table 2 prior to discharge to any adjoining drainage system.
- Water quality modelling undertaken to support development proposals within the Precinct shall utilise the latest version of MUSIC and be in line with the Draft NSW MUSIC Modelling Guidelines, Sydney Metropolitan Catchment Management Authority, 2010, utilising the modelling parameters in Tables 3 and 4.
- For developments generating oils and grease, the additional objective of no visible oils for flows up to 50% of the one-year Average Recurrence Interval peak flow shall be achieved.
- A Water Sensitive Urban Design strategy is to be prepared for all development that provides for sustainable and integrated management of land and water resources, taking into account water quality and stream erosivity objectives, together with attenuating flow rates and runoff volumes to acceptable levels following urban development. Water management performance objectives are set out in Table 2.
- Water Sensitive Urban Design elements are to be designed and constructed in accordance with the following publications:
- Adoption Guidelines for Stormwater Biofiltration Systems - Cities as Water Supply Catchments, Sustainable Technologies (CRC for Water Sensitive Cities, 2015 or later)
- Australian Runoff Quality (Engineers Australia 2005)
- Water Sensitive Urban Design Technical Guidelines for Western Sydney (NSW Government Stormwater Trust and Upper Parramatta River Catchment Trust, May 2004)
- As part of a Water Sensitive Urban Design strategy, developments are to install rainwater tanks for water supply demand such as outdoor use, laundries and toilets. With the exception of

<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 29 -->

detached residential dwellings, a water balance assessment is to be undertaken for the development and rainwater tanks appropriately sized to cater for the water use demand. The following provisions apply:


## Detached residential dwellings

- Minimum 3,000 litre rainwater tank for toilet flushing and external uses is required. Larger tanks and use for filling of swimming pools is permitted.

## Multi dwelling housing

- Minimum 3,000 litre rainwater tank per proposed dwelling or as defined by a detailed water balance assessment for the development is required.
- Rainwater tanks may be connected to toilets, laundries and external uses including the filling of swimming pools.

## Residential flat buildings

- The required rainwater tank volume is to be determined by a detailed water balance assessment.
- Rainwater tanks are to be used for external uses and other purposes such as wash down bays and laundry facilities.
- Rainwater tanks are to be provided with potable water trickle top-up with a back flow prevention device, complying with Sydney Water requirements.
- In accordance with the recommendations made in the publication 'Guidance on the Use of Rainwater Tanks' (enHealth, Commonwealth Government 2004), diversion of the 'first flush' of up to 180 litres is to be incorporated into the design of the rainwater tank and associated plumbing based on a minimum first flush of 1L/m 2 of roof area.
- Any discharge to, or construction within the Elizabeth Macarthur riparian corridor may require the approval of NSW Office of Water, under the Water Management Act 2000.
- The natural form, characteristics and function of waterways, including riparian land, are to be retained, restored, protected and enhanced wherever possible.
- Waterway rehabilitation and construction works are to apply 'Best Practice' combination of soft and hard engineering techniques establishing a water sensitive, geomorphically stable, diverse and functional waterway corridor that addresses urban influences and considers the immediate waterway corridor and aquatic systems both upstream and downstream of a subject site.
As a minimum, waterway design and construction should follow the principles and guidelines in the Constructed Wetlands Manual (Department of Land and Water Conservation, NSW 1998) and A Rehabilitation Manual for Australian Streams (Cooperative Research Centre for Catchment Hydrology, 2000).

- During construction, water shall not collect or pond on or near the railway infrastructure. No run-off from the development shall discharge onto Transport for NSW or Sydney Metro owned land, the Sydney Metro rail corridor, into the Sydney Metro stormwater system or into the track drainage system during construction. Refer to the Sydney Metro Guidelines for more information.
- Risk assessment should consider the full range of flooding (not only the 1% AEP flood), including events up to the Probable Maximum Flood (PMF).
- Risk assessment should have regard to flood warning and evacuation demand on existing and future access/egress routes. Consideration should also be given to the impacts of localised flooding on evacuation routes.
- Future development should ensure that self-evacuation of the community is achievable in a manner which is consistent with the NSW SES's principles for evacuation.
- Future development must not conflict with the NSW SES's flood response and evacuation strategy for the existing community.
- Evacuation must not require people to drive or walk through flood water.

# 4.4 Subdivision and Earthworks


## Objectives

- To minimise topsoil and vegetation removal and 'land-shaping' on land where residential subdivisions are being constructed.
- Subdivisions provide a landform that is capable of supporting a range of residential, business and industrial uses.
- To ensure development visually integrates with the surrounding environment.

## Controls

- Earthworks shall be minimised to locations where the construction of roads require earthworks to be undertaken or filling adjacent to Elizabeth Macarthur Creek (refer to Integrated Water Management and Cut and Fill Sections of this DCP).
- All proposed public open space areas are to be fenced and are not to be disturbed or used for any purpose during the construction of a subdivision.
- Subdivision applications must provide a plan showing the existing pre-development and proposed finished ground levels to enable an assessment of the extent of earthworks proposed

<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 32 -->

and assessment of the relationship between the finished road levels and proposed building platform levels.


# 4.5 Cut and Fill


# Objectives

- To minimise the impact of earthworks on the stormwater regime, salinity and groundwater.
- To ensure the extent of cut and fill required for large scale development does not detract from the appearance and design.
- To ensure development visually integrates with the surrounding environment.
- To minimise the risks and associated impacts of contaminated land and to ensure land is appropriately stabilised and retained.
- To ensure that cut and fill does not encroach within, or adversely affect the efficiency, integrity and stability of any open space area.

## Controls

- The filling of land adjacent to the Elizabeth Macarthur Creek Corridor may be required to facilitate the urban development of the Precinct and will only be permitted after consultation with NSW Office of Water (or any other relevant Government Agency) and to the subsequent levels provided. Justification for any proposed changes to land levels provided is required and is to be supported by a flood assessment that takes into account the cumulative impact of flooding behaviour, and associated risks caused by individual developments.
- In the areas of fill relevant provisions of Council's Flood Controlled Land DCP are to be applied, with reference to the Integrated Water Management Section of this DCP.
- A Fill Plan must be prepared.
- All cut and fill works shall be in accordance with Council's Design Guidelines Subdivisions/Developments and Works Specification Subdivisions/Developments.
- All landfilled areas must comprise clean material free from contamination. Imported material shall be certified 'Virgin Excavated Natural Material (VENM)'.
- Landfilled areas must be suitably compacted and stabilised with density tests to verify that compaction was achieved in accordance with Council requirements.
- Embankment batters shall be provided in accordance with Council's Design Guidelines Subdivisions/Developments.
- Embankment batters and retaining walls are to be landscaped to reduce erosion and provide a suitable screen. They should be vegetated preferably with native ground covers and small native trees with mature height of up to 10m.
- Development shall comply with the provisions of State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 (formerly State Environmental Planning Policy No. 55 - Remediation of Land).
- Development shall comply with the Acid Sulfate Soils provisions of LEP 2019.

# 4.6 Ecologically Sustainable Development


# Objectives

- Building designs are innovative and sustainable to reduce the reliance on, and consumption of, fossil fuels and potable water supplies.
- Development adapts to climate change.
- Developments contribute to improved quality of life, health and well-being of the community.

<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 33 -->

- The design, construction and operation of development minimises adverse impacts on the natural environment.
- Use landscape treatments to improve amenity for people using open space.

# Controls

- Residential flat buildings, townhouses and terraces built as a development lot should achieve a minimum 5 star NatHERS energy rating for each dwelling unit.
- Development other than residential should achieve a minimum 5 star Green Star Design and as Built rating, respectively.
- Building operation should achieve a minimum 4.5 star base building and tenancy NABERS Energy rating, where applicable.
- The incorporation of green walls and roofs into the design of commercial and residential buildings is encouraged. Where suitable, building facades should incorporate vertical landscaping features to soften the visual bulk of buildings and to improve streetscape appeal.
- Canopy trees are to be planted within deep soil setbacks of developments, street verges and medians to provide shade and reduce pavement surface temperatures. Understorey planting and permeable surfaces should also be provided where possible to reduce the extent of paved area and to enhance the amenity of the streetscape environment.
- Buildings are encouraged to incorporate a trigeneration energy facility that provides energyefficient power, heating and air conditioning for use on site.
- Building designs are to:
- Maximise the use of natural light and cross ventilation
- Reduce the reliance on mechanical heating and cooling through the use of eaves, awnings, good insulation and landscaping
- Include energy efficient light fittings and water fittings
- Allow for separate metering of water and energy usage for commercial and multi-unit tenancies.
- Provide green roofs and walls wherever practical to mitigate the loss of green canopy and vegetation as a result of development.
- Building facades should also incorporate vertical landscaping features to soften the visual bulk of buildings and to improve streetscape appeal.

<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 34 -->


# 4.7 Ecology and Riparian Corridors


# Objectives

- To protect and enhance areas of significant native vegetation.
- To protect and enhance wildlife habitat.
- To protect and enhance the integrity and environmental functionality of the Elizabeth Macarthur Creek Riparian Corridor.

# Controls

- Wherever practical, development within the Precincts should be sited to minimise impacts on the existing vegetation and avoid removal of significant trees.
- A site specific Vegetation Management Plan (VMP) may need to be prepared and implemented for Elizabeth Macarthur Creek. Should this be required, this plan is to be lodged with development applications for development on land within the riparian corridor (being within 20m of top of bank as identified in Figure 25 ), and approved prior to the commencement of construction works on this land. The requirement for a VMP is to be determined in consultation with Council Officers.
- Should a VMP not be required, landscaping along the riparian corridor should still feature native riparian plantings that are reflective of the riparian character and existing vegetation community profile.
- The VMP is to be prepared in accordance with Council's relevant guidelines and based on standard vegetation management actions.
- The VMP is to provide for a minimum 2 year monitoring and maintenance period for the rehabilitated riparian area and other revegetation following final planting.

<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 35 -->

![page 35 img 1 (1230x841)](images/the-hills-development-control-plan-2012/p0035-066db47cf60c.png)


*Figure 25:*


## Location of Riparian Corridor

# 4.8 Safety and Security


# Objectives

- To provide high levels of property safety as well as personal comfort and safety.
- To minimise opportunities for criminal and anti-social behaviour through urban design.

# Controls

- Development is to address the principles of Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design.
Note: Consideration shall also be given to The Hills Shire Council's Policy Designing Safer Communities, Safer by Design Guidelines (June 2002).


# 4.9 Heritage (Aboriginal and Non-Aboriginal)


# Objectives

- Development is designed and located to protect Aboriginal sites and archaeological relics by minimising the likelihood of disturbance.
- Development is appropriately designed with regard to sensitive and direct interfaces with heritage sites.
- Development is sited to minimise adverse impacts on the significance of the heritage items.

## Controls - Aboriginal Heritage

- An Aboriginal Due Diligence Report is required for each major development site/subdivision and must be prepared in accordance with the Due Diligence Code of Practice for the Protection of Aboriginal Objects in NSW.
- Where a Due Diligence Report identifies the presence or likely presence of any Aboriginal sites or relics on or near the subject development site, further Aboriginal Cultural / Archaeological Assessment by a suitably qualified person must be undertaken. Where a site is identified as significant, a letter from the relevant Aboriginal Lands Council is required to be submitted expressing support or recommendations for the subdivision proposal.
- Consideration must be given to Heritage NSW's Guidelines for conducting Aboriginal cultural heritage assessments and associated Aboriginal community consultation processes.

## Controls -Non-Aboriginal Heritage

- Development at, or within the vicinity of the heritage item (I28), being Windsor Road from Baulkham Hills to Box Hill, must have regard to Part C Section 4 - Heritage of DCP 2012.

# 4.10 Wind


# Objectives

- To allow for cooling summer breezes to move through the precinct.
- To ensure the built form does not provide adverse wind conditions which will impact upon the amenity of pedestrian comfort in streets and public open spaces.
- The built form does not adversely impact upon the amenity of residents in common open spaces.

<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 37 -->


# Controls

- Built form is to demonstrate that the passage of cooling summer breezes will not be impacted.
- Buildings 8 or more storeys in height (or over 25 metres) require wind tunnel testing, irrespective of whether they are built to the street frontage or not, which demonstrates the following:
- In open areas to which people have access, the annual maximum gust speed should not exceed 23 metres per second.
- In walkways, pedestrian transit areas, streets where pedestrians do not generally stop, sit, stand, window shop and the like, annual maximum gust speed should not exceed 16 metres per second.
- In areas where pedestrians are involved in stationary short-exposure activities such as window shopping, standing or sitting (including areas such as bus stops, public open space and private open space), the annual maximum gust speed should not exceed 13 metres per second.
- In areas for stationary long-exposure activity, such as outdoor dining, the annual maximum gust speed should not exceed 10 metres per second.
- The report is to be prepared by a suitably qualified engineer.

<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 38 -->


# 5 Residential Flat Buildings and Shop Top Housing


# 5.1 Site Requirements

The Hills LEP 2019 Clause 8.2 (Minimum lot sizes residential flat buildings and shop top housing) specifies the minimum lot size for residential flat buildings in the R4 High Density Residential zone and R1 General Residential zone.


# Objectives

- To encourage the amalgamation of sites and discourage the creation of isolated development sites.
- To provide sufficient space for landscaping that will complement the building form and enhance the landscape character of the street.
- Development sites have sufficient area to provide adequate access, parking, landscaping and building separation.

# Controls

- Development sites shall have a minimum road frontage of 30m.
- Development sites shall have a minimum site depth of 40m.
- Residential flat buildings and shop top housing are to have a frontage (address) to the street and are not to be located on battle-axe allotments or rely on right of access arrangements for access to a public road.
- The site coverage of future development shall not exceed 50% of the site area (excluding land to be dedicated or acquired or a public purpose).
Note : Determination of site cover includes driveways, footpaths and other impervious surfaces.


## Note: Isolation of Lots and Orderly Development

The creation of isolated sites is not desirable and should be avoided where possible. Where a property is likely to be isolated by a development and it cannot be demonstrated that the site can be developed to its full potential, applicants should provide documentary evidence that a genuine and reasonable attempt has been made to purchase the isolated site based on a fair market value.

Where a development may result in the creation of an isolated lot/s, the applicant should demonstrate that:

-  Negotiations for amalgamation of sites commenced early, prior to the lodgement of a development application;
-  If negotiations are not successful, details of the negotiations should be provided with the development application submission, including at least one recent independent valuation (which considers the property as being part of a complying amalgamated site) and include other reasonable expenses likely to be incurred by the owner of the isolated property in the sale of the property; and

<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 39 -->

-  The orderly development of the isolated site can be achieved that is consistent with the provisions of The Hills LEP and DCP. This should include the applicant providing an envelope for that site, indicating height, building form, setbacks and separations (building and basement) sufficient to understand the relationship between the proposed development and the isolated site and the streetscape implications.
-  The development of an isolated site should not detract from the character of the streetscape and is to achieve a satisfactory level of amenity, including solar access, visual and acoustic privacy.

# 5.2 Setbacks (Building and Upper Level)


# Objectives

- To provide strong definition to the public domain and create a consistent streetscape.
- To set taller building elements back from the street to reduce building scale and bulk and enable adequate sunlight access to the public domain.
- To provide articulation zones to complement building mass and emphasise key design elements such as entrance points and respond to environmental conditions including solar access, noise, privacy and views.
- To ensure adequate separation between buildings on different sites to alleviate amenity impacts, including privacy, daylight access, acoustic control and natural ventilation.
- To facilitate a landscaped streetscape that can accommodate larger trees.

# Controls

- Building setbacks are to comply with those shown in Figure 26 and Table 5 below.
- Buildings on street corners are to address both street frontages, with corners emphasised by appropriate architectural treatment.
- Future developments must ensure minimum setbacks provided to the Sydney Metro North West Line overhead viaduct / rail corridor are consistent with the considerations set out in the Sydney Metro Guidelines.

# 5.3 Open Space and Landscaping


# Objectives

- To maximise opportunities for landscaping, including the retention and/or planting of trees within deep soil areas to ensure a high level of amenity.
- To assist with the management of water quality.
- To provide communal open space for the enjoyment of residents.
- Communal open spaces:
- o Are accessible, usable and safe;
- o Enhance the attractiveness of the development;
- o Provide opportunities for social interaction; and
- o Create pleasantly shaded outdoor areas.
- To ensure development sites have sufficient space for landscaping that will complement the building form and enhance the landscape character of the street.

<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 42 -->


# Controls


# Landscaping

- A minimum of 45% of the site area shall comprise Landscaped Area (as defined below, noting the calculation of Landscaped Area excludes the building footprint, roads, access driveways, parking and other hard paved areas etc.). Terraces and patios within 1m of natural ground level shall be included in the calculation of Landscape Area (as defined below).
Note: Landscaped Area means a part of a site used for growing plants, grasses and trees, but does not include any building, structure or hard paved area.

- Landscaped areas are to have a minimum width of 2m. Areas less than 2m in width will be excluded from the calculation of Landscaped Area.
- Native ground covers and grasses are to be used in garden beds and path surrounds (turf is to be confined to useable outdoor areas).

## Roof Gardens and Planting on Structures

- Green walls are encouraged on podium walls along active frontages to soften the interface between future development and the public realm.
- Rooftop gardens must be adequately enclosed and accessible to occupants of the development.
- The design of exterior private open spaces such as roof top gardens is to address visual and acoustic privacy, safety, security, and wind effects.
- Where roof gardens and green walls are provided, consideration should be given to the Urban Green Cover in NSW - Technical Guidelines, published by the Office of Environment and Heritage.

## Communal Open Space

- A minimum of 10m 2 per dwelling shall be provided as communal open space.
- A minimum of 25% of the required communal open space must be located at ground level in a singular large parcel.
- External (outside) common open space areas are to be capable of accommodating substantial vegetation and are to be designed to incorporate active and passive recreation facilities (such as seating, shade structures, BBQs, children's play equipment and swimming pools).
- External (outside) common open space areas are to be located and designed to:
- Be seen from the street between buildings;
- Provide for active and passive recreation needs of all residents;
- Provide landscaping;
- Present as a private area for use by residents only;
- Include passive surveillance from adjacent internal living areas and/or pathways;
- Have a northerly aspect where possible; and
- Be in addition to any public thoroughfares.
- Internal open space areas are to provide opportunities for larger communal gathering and/or active recreation (i.e. kitchen facilities, tables and chairs, small-scale gymnasium, health studio or swimming pools).

<!-- SRC: 44-part-d-section-26-bella-vista-and-kellyville-station-precincts.pdf | PAGE: 43 -->

- Plant species appropriate to the context and the specific microclimate within the development are to be selected to maximise use of endemic and native species and opportunities for urban biodiversity.
- Drought tolerant plant species, and species that enhance habitat and ecology, are to be prioritised.
- Landscape design is to be integrated with water and stormwater management.
